aerostatic-lift-budget.title: What Holds Up a Living Balloon
aerostatic-lift-budget.subtitle: Lift is bought by the cubic metre; the skin is paid for by the square metre

hint.flying: Above the crossing the cube beats the square: every metre of extra diameter adds more lift than skin. This is why an aerostat has no choice but to be enormous, and why the caravan animals can carry a village while the field-guide drifter cannot carry anyone.
hint.grounded: Below the crossing the square wins. The wall and the living tissue behind it weigh more than the displaced air will hold, so this animal cannot lift even itself — no arrangement of gas will save it. There are no sparrow-sized balloon animals for exactly this reason.

aria.flying: Gross lift curve above the overhead curve, leaving spare payload
aria.grounded: Overhead curve above the gross lift curve, so the envelope cannot lift itself

readout.minimumDiameter: needs at least {d} m to fly

airRegime.title: The texture of the air
airRegime.subtitle: Reynolds number and flow regimes
airRegime.hint: Air is a thick syrup to a bug, and a clean stream to an eagle. Denser air on Pandora pushes fliers into a cleaner, more efficient aerodynamic regime.
airRegime.viscousDesc: Sticky, turbulent flow. High drag, stalling.
airRegime.transitionalDesc: Flow begins to attach, but unsteady.

allometry.title: Bone Stress & Allometry
allometry.infoAllometric: Allometry: Bones thicken non-linearly to support the cubed weight, maintaining skeletal integrity.
allometry.infoIsometric: Isometry: Linear scaling. Volume (mass) increases by 8x while bone cross-section only increases by 4x, risking fracture.

biohydrogen-ledger.title: Where the Lifting Gas Comes From
biohydrogen-ledger.subtitle: Making hydrogen is easy; a gut that keeps any is the hard part

stage.evolved: {v} m³ of hydrogen evolved per day

verdict.holding: The envelope gains {pct}% of its volume per day
verdict.sinking: The envelope loses {pct}% of its volume per day

biohydrogen-ledger.ceilingNote: At the thermodynamic ceiling of four hydrogen per sugar, the same meal would net {v} m³.

hint.earthLike: A cow's rumen evolves cubic metres of hydrogen a day and exhales essentially none. Methanogens and sulfate reducers consume it the instant it appears — hydrogen is the currency of the gut, spent as fast as it is earned. Route that stream into a bladder and there is nothing left to route.
hint.medusoid: Suppress the microbes that eat hydrogen and the same fermentation suddenly has an output. This — not the chemistry of making the gas — is the one biological novelty a living aerostat actually requires. Everything else it does, animals on Earth already do.

aria.earthLike: Almost the entire hydrogen stream consumed by microbes before reaching the bladder
aria.medusoid: Most of the hydrogen stream reaching the bladder, with a narrow leakage band

readout.rentNote: prey needed just to break even

burning-wing.title: How Long Can a Burning Wing Fly?
burning-wing.subtitle: The wing stops flying long before it stops existing
burning-wing.aria: Loss of control at {loc} seconds against burn-through at {burn} seconds
burning-wing.hint: Control goes at about {loc} seconds, while burning through the membrane takes some {burn} — and {water} percent of that longer budget is spent boiling water out of living tissue. Water is a superb heat sink, so the fire needs a long time to finish the wing. It needs almost none to ruin it: collagen unwinds at 58–65 °C and contracts hard along its fibres, and a puckered membrane on one wing is an uncommanded roll the animal cannot trim out.

readout.biotThick: Thick enough to hold a gradient

cohesionTension.title: Cohesion-Tension
cohesionTension.subtitle: Water column tension under transpiration pull
cohesionTension.hint: Water has no pump: leaves evaporate water (transpiration), pulling the molecules behind them. High sun or excessive height stretches the water column. Exceed the threshold, and the column snaps, blocking flow.

combustion-budget.title: Does This Air Want to Burn?
combustion-budget.subtitle: A flame survives only while it releases heat faster than its surroundings take it away

loss.diluent: Heat soaked up by the diluent gas
loss.convective: Heat stripped by the moving air

combustion-budget.aria: Flame at {speed} percent of Earth burning velocity and {temp} kelvin

hint.readily: This air supports fire much as Earth's does. Enough oxygen to keep the radical chain branching, little enough diluent that most of the reaction heat stays in the flame.
hint.reluctant: Fire still takes, but grudgingly. Carbon dioxide is a triatomic molecule with more ways to store energy than nitrogen has, so it drinks reaction heat and drops the flame temperature — and a cooler flame ignites its neighbours more slowly.
hint.marginal: Barely combustible. Between a thin oxygen supply and a heavy heat-absorbing diluent, the flame can no longer heat the fuel ahead of it fast enough to keep itself fed.
hint.blownOff: Blown out. The airstream now carries heat off faster than the reaction can replace it — reactants sweep through the flame zone before they finish reacting, and the flame simply stops. This is why an unshielded torch cannot survive at flying speed.

readout.verdictNote: How readily fire takes and spreads

consciousBottleneck.title: The conscious bottleneck
consciousBottleneck.subtitle: Eleven million bits in; a few dozen bits of self out
consciousBottleneck.compressionNote: sensation thrown away per bit kept
consciousBottleneck.aria: The senses pour in eleven million bits per second; only {conscious} reaches awareness — a {compression}-fold compression.
consciousBottleneck.hint: Your senses pour ~11 Mb/s into the nervous system, yet the stream that reaches awareness — the self that thinks and remembers — runs at a mere handful of bits per second. Slide that rate and watch a whole lifetime of selfhood collapse to mere tens of gigabits: small enough, at last, to send across the bond in a single night.

cooper-pair.title: Cooper Pair
cooper-pair.info: Two electrons that ought to repel are bound at a distance by a wake in the ion lattice: the first drags the heavy positive ions inward, the second rides the fleeting pocket of positive charge left behind. With zero net spin the pair acts as a boson and can condense into one shared quantum state — the basis of BCS superconductivity. Warm past the critical temperature and lattice jitter shakes the bond apart.
cooper-pair.bound: Bound as one — a zero-spin boson

critical-temperature.title: Critical Temperature
critical-temperature.info: The temperature Tc below which a material turns superconducting. An ordinary metal's resistance eases down smoothly as it cools; a superconductor's falls off a cliff to exactly zero the instant it crosses Tc. Mercury needs liquid helium, the ceramic YBCO reaches liquid nitrogen — and unobtanium's whole fantasy is to push that same cliff up to a warm Pandoran afternoon.

diamagnetism.title: Diamagnetism
diamagnetism.info: The tendency of matter to weakly repel a magnetic field, born of electron orbital motion. In ordinary stuff — graphite, water, living tissue — it is so faint it takes a huge field to levitate a frog. A superconductor is the limiting case: a perfect diamagnet that expels the field entirely and floats even in a weak one. Pick a material and dial the field to watch its response reverse and grow.

dynamicSoaring.title: Dynamic Soaring
dynamicSoaring.subtitle: Harvesting kinetic energy from wind gradients
dynamicSoaring.hint: Dynamic soaring works by flying between different wind speeds. By climbing into fast wind (ascent) and diving into slow wind near the sea (descent), a bird extracts energy from the wind shear, staying aloft indefinitely without flapping.

edge-toughness.title: The Sharpest Edge Is the Most Fragile
edge-toughness.subtitle: What lets a material part cleanly is what stops it surviving a second blow
edge-toughness.aria: Edge sharpness plotted against fracture toughness for five weapon materials

hint.glass: An edge a few nanometres across, an order of magnitude finer than surgical steel, and it costs nothing but a well-aimed blow to make. The price is written in the toughness figure: with no crystal planes and no plastic give, a crack that starts anywhere runs everywhere. Superb on soft tissue, finished the moment it meets bone.
hint.chert: Heating siliceous stone to a few hundred degrees drives out water between the crystals and lets it flake almost as cleanly as glass, while keeping nearly twice the toughness. The first material improvement in history that was purely thermal.
hint.bone: Blunt by any of these standards, and by far the most forgiving. Bone is a composite, so a crack in it has to fight its way through mineral and protein in turn — which is exactly what makes it the right choice for a shaft or a haft rather than a point.
hint.steel: Blunter than glass by more than tenfold, and forty times harder to break. Metal deforms before it parts, so a crack has to keep being fed. The catch is the furnace: this edge is unavailable to anyone without roughly 1,500 °C.
hint.salvage: The toughest thing on the plot, obtainable with no furnace at all. Hammer aerospace alloy cold and it hardens as its internal dislocations tangle; warm it to a few hundred degrees and they untangle again, restoring workability. Never molten, never cast — and never as sharp as glass.

readout.edgeNote: How fine an edge it takes

flierShowdown.title: The giants, to scale
flierShowdown.subtitle: Comparing Earth's largest to Pandora's everyday fliers
flierShowdown.hint: Quetzalcoatlus is the absolute largest creature Earth ever put in the air. The mountain banshee matches it. The toruk doubles it.

flightLab.title: The wall for fliers
flightLab.subtitle: Where power demanded crosses power supplied
flightLab.hint: The teal curve is what muscles can supply. The amber curve is what flight demands. They must cross, setting a maximum mass. Drop Pandora's gravity and thicken its air, and watch the demand curve slide down — pushing the crossing point to a much heavier animal.

flux-pinning.title: Flux Pinning
flux-pinning.info: Why a hover becomes a lock. In a type-II superconductor the field pierces the bulk as quantized threads, and a free thread drifts and dissipates. So each lattice defect — a missing atom, a void, a grain boundary — becomes a trap: a thread's normal core drops into it like a key into a lock and stays. Drag the disc and the pinned threads haul it back. More defects, more grip — the trick unobtanium's void-riddled quasicrystal plays on a planet.

froudeDial.title: Froude gait dial
froudeDial.hint: At the same leg length, Pandora's lower gravity pulls every gait transition down to a lower speed. The pa'li breaks into its efficient spring-loaded gaits sooner - and each footfall lands softer for it.

hallelujah-mountains.title: Hallelujah Mountains
hallelujah-mountains.info: The lab disc, scaled to a planet. Pandora's floating mountains are a superconducting unobtanium core sewn into the Flux Vortex — the overlapping fields of the moon and the gas giant Polyphemus. Drag the mountain and the pinned flux threads stretch and pull it home; let go and it settles, because the pinned core (pulling up) and heavy ballast rock (pulling down) act as two opposed springs into a passive, self-correcting equilibrium.
hallelujah-mountains.pinnedPullsBack: Pinned — the flux threads pull it home
hallelujah-mountains.stableEquilibrium: Locked in a stable, self-correcting equilibrium

hydraulicLimit.title: How tall can a tree get?
hydraulicLimit.subtitle: Drag the height up to see how much the water column stretches
hydraulicLimit.turgorNote: How well the topmost leaves can still fill with water and grow.
hydraulicLimit.snapNote: Past the ceiling the water column snaps — the top can no longer drink.
hydraulicLimit.verdictOk: The crown is still paying its way: water reaches the top under survivable tension.
hydraulicLimit.verdictOver: Beyond what the plumbing allows here. On Earth this is impossible; on Pandora, lower gravity and a CO2-rich, humid atmosphere lift the ceiling — straining toward Hometree's scale, not sailing past it.
hydraulicLimit.hint: A tree has no pump: it drinks by pulling an unbroken thread of water up its wood, powered only by evaporation from its leaves. The taller it grows, the harder the top must pull, until the leaf cells can no longer fill — Koch & Sillett (2004) put Earth's ceiling near 130 m. Switch to Pandora and watch lower gravity and dense, carbon-rich air move that ceiling.

hydrogen-flammability-window.title: How Wide Is the Window to Burn?
hydrogen-flammability-window.subtitle: Hydrogen ignites across a huge range — until something drinks the heat

hint.flammable: Hydrogen's band is extraordinarily wide and needs almost nothing to light it — an unfelt spark will do. Carbon dioxide narrows the window from the rich end, because a triatomic molecule stores more of the reaction's heat than nitrogen can. Pandora's air is genuinely more forgiving than Earth's here. It is not forgiving enough to make an ember arrow safe.
hint.inert: Past this much diluent the two limits meet and the window closes: no proportion of hydrogen and this air will carry a flame at all. Fire suppression works by reaching this point, not by removing every spark.

aria.flammable: Flammable window from {lean} to {rich} percent hydrogen
aria.inert: Flammable window closed; no mixture ignites

readout.mieNote: a static discharge is far more
readout.safeNote: the diluent has closed the window
readout.ignitableNote: an ember is more than enough

meissner-effect.title: Meissner Effect
meissner-effect.info: The magnetic mirror switching on. Above Tc a disc is an ordinary conductor and a magnet's field threads straight through it. Cool it past Tc and lossless surface currents spring up, holding exactly the pattern needed to cancel the field inside — every line is thrown out, the interior falls to zero, and the magnet is pushed up into a hover. This is the lift: pure repulsion, the beautiful but twitchy half Earnshaw's theorem forbids from being stable.

occamsRazor.title: Occam's Razor
occamsRazor.subtitle: Weighing competing explanations
occamsRazor.hint: Adjust the number of unproven assumptions. The razor shaves away the theory that demands too many miracles.
occamsRazor.noteA: Relies on fewer leaps of faith.
occamsRazor.noteB: Relies on fewer leaps of faith.
occamsRazor.noteTie: Cannot distinguish based on simplicity alone.

assumptionsList.active: Banshee was active in this area
assumptionsList.paint: Drones leaked glowing cyan chemical paint
assumptionsList.stealth: Stealth drone intentionally snapped twigs to mark path
assumptionsList.wind: Heavy storm wind carried the drones here undetected

quantum-locking.title: Quantum Locking
quantum-locking.info: Flux pinning seen from outside. Once the threads pin, the disc is not resting on the field — it is sewn into it, fixed at whatever position and tilt you left it. Rotate the whole magnet track and the disc rides with it at the same gap and angle, until at full inversion it hangs underneath, refusing to fall. It is not balancing — a balanced magnet would slide off the instant you tipped it. It is locked, rigid in three dimensions, hands-off and powerless.
quantum-locking.hangsBeneath: Inverted — it hangs beneath the track

radiant-dose.title: Fire Reaches What It Never Touches
radiant-dose.subtitle: Radiated heat climbs as the fourth power of temperature and thins with distance
radiant-dose.aria: Radiant flux of {flux} kilowatts per square metre at {dist} metres from the flame

hint.none: Below the threshold where anything happens. Heat is arriving, but slowly enough that skin and fuel shed it as fast as it lands.
hint.pain: Enough to hurt within about half a minute, and nothing more. Sunlight at its fiercest delivers roughly half this.
hint.blister: The escape threshold. Skin blisters in ten to fifteen seconds here, which is why fire crews treat this flux as the line you do not stand behind.
hint.ignition: Now dry wood and cloth catch from a spark or a stray ember — no flame need reach them. This is the flux that spreads a fire through a forest, delivered across open air.
hint.autoignition: Hot enough that dry fuel bursts alight with no ignition source at all, in seconds. Nothing organic survives standing in this.

readout.outcomeNote: The highest threshold this flux clears

scaleUp.title: The square-cube scaling trap
scaleUp.subtitle: Scale an animal up and watch mass outrun wing area
scaleUp.hint: Double the length, and you get 4× the wing area to lift 8× the mass. The 'wing loading' (mass per unit wing area) climbs relentlessly, forcing the animal to fly faster and faster just to stay in the air. Eventually, the stall speed exceeds what muscles can deliver.

shannonChannel.title: Shannon's channel, made playable
shannonChannel.subtitle: C = B · log₂(1 + S/N)
shannonChannel.aria: Channel capacity {capacity}; the chosen payload takes {time} to cross.
shannonChannel.hint: Drag bandwidth and watch the answer move in great linear strides; drag the signal-to-noise ratio and watch it barely budge. Bandwidth is the precious resource — raw power is almost useless. Then send a whole connectome down the biological cable and see why an overnight transfer of a mind is impossible the maximalist way, and merely extravagant the minimalist way.

shannonEntropy.title: Shannon Entropy
shannonEntropy.subtitle: Uncertainty and information content of a biased coin flip
shannonEntropy.hint: At p = 0.5, the coin is perfectly fair and unpredictability is maximized at 1.0 bit of entropy per flip. At p = 0.0 or 1.0, the outcome is completely certain, carrying 0 bits of information because you gain no new knowledge when it lands.

squareCubeLaw.title: The Square-Cube Law
squareCubeLaw.subtitle: How mass outruns surface area during scaling
squareCubeLaw.hint: Double the height, and you get 4x the muscle/bone cross-section but 8x the mass to support. Bone stress increases linearly with size. That is why Na'vi have carbon-fiber reinforced bones, and why giant terrestrial animals cannot exist with standard human proportions.

superconductivity.title: Superconductivity
superconductivity.info: The current that never stops. Start a current in a loop of ordinary metal and resistance bleeds it away in a heartbeat; start one in a superconducting ring below Tc and it runs — no battery, no voltage, no measured loss — as long as anyone has watched. Cool the ring and the current persists forever; warm it above Tc and resistance returns, the glow dims, the current decays. Onnes found this in mercury in 1911 — the first of the chapter's two miracles.

superconductor.title: Superconductor cool-down
superconductor.hint: Drop the temperature below Tc: resistance falls straight to zero and the magnet locks, hanging in mid-air.
superconductor.dragToMove: DRAG BLOCK TO MOVE ALONG MAGNETIC TRACK
superconductor.lowerToLevitate: LOWER TEMPERATURE BELOW Tc TO LEVITATE

superposition.title: Superposition
superposition.info: Stratigraphy's founding rule, obvious once said yet quietly powerful: in an undisturbed sequence of sedimentary rock, the layer beneath is always older than the one above, because it was laid down first. Scrub deposition time and the column builds from the floor up; click any bed to see its place in the order. No absolute dates needed — superposition alone lets you read the before-and-after of a planet's history straight off a cliff face.
superposition.lowerIsOlder: Lower layer is older — it was laid down first

torukFlight.title: Toruk Flight Synthesizer
torukFlight.subtitle: Turn on Pandora's three physical 'cheats' to get Toruk airborne
torukFlight.hint: Activate the necessary conditions to make Toruk's flight viable.
torukFlight.failDesc: Standard Earth physics. Toruk is far too heavy to fly or launch.
torukFlight.successDesc: All three Pandoran physics cheats combined. The lift is higher, the weight is lower, and the launch muscles are maximized. Toruk flies.

towed-aerostat-power.title: A Balloon Has No Course
towed-aerostat-power.subtitle: Drifting is free; going anywhere costs the cube of the speed
towed-aerostat-power.xAxis: Speed relative to the surrounding air (m/s)

hint.drifting: At zero the aerostat is simply part of the air. It feels no wind, needs no power, and can drift for months — but it also has no rudder, because a rudder needs something to push against. Altitude is the only steering a free balloon owns.
hint.feasible: A handful of tugs can manage this. Note how gently the caravan moves: walking pace, and it stays walking pace, because the next increment of speed costs far more than the last.
hint.impossible: Now the arithmetic breaks. Power rises as the cube of speed, so this pace would need a flock no clan could feed. A living airship is not slow because nobody thought of going faster — it is slow because faster is unaffordable.

towed-aerostat-power.aria: About {n} tugs required at {v} metres per second

readout.cubeNote: doubling speed costs eight times this
readout.perAnimal: at about 2 kW of thrust each

type-ii-superconductor.title: Type-II Superconductor
type-ii-superconductor.info: The superconductor that lets the field in — on its own terms. A type-I metal expels everything until the field wins and it collapses, all-or-nothing. A type-II has two thresholds: below Hc1 full expulsion, above Hc2 it dies, but in the wide mixed state between it admits the field as a forest of quantized Abrikosov vortices while the bulk stays superconducting. That tolerance for high fields is why every practical superconductor is type-II — and where flux pinning gets its hooks.
